Description: Surrogate key referenced by every audit column.
Why: AC-US-00-007-5: every decision names who made it, which needs a stable user id.

Description: Sign-in name, unique ignoring case.
Why: AC-US-00-011-1: a seeded staff account signs in by name.

Description: Name shown in the decision log.
Why: AC-US-00-007-5: the log shows who decided.

Description: staff or verifier, the only two roles in the product.
Why: AC-US-00-011-3: a verifier is refused a staff-only action, so the role is stored.

Description: Argon2id hash of the password, never the password.
Why: AC-US-00-011-1: sign-in checks a password, and a leak must not reveal it.

Description: False blocks sign-in and revokes sessions without deleting audit history.
Why: Rule: users are deactivated, never deleted, because decisions reference them (AC-US-00-007-5).

Description: Incremented to end every session of this user at once.
Why: Rule: logout everywhere is one increment (auth skill).

Description: Last successful sign-in.
Why: AC-US-00-011-1: sign-in is recorded for the account.

Description: When the account was seeded.
Why: Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Last change to this row.
Why: Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Surrogate key.
Why: AC-US-00-011-1: a sign-in creates a session.

Description: The user this session belongs to.
Why: AC-US-00-011-2: the session carries the verifier role. CASCADE because a session means nothing without its user.

Description: SHA-256 of the random cookie token, so a database leak yields no usable cookie.
Why: Rule: store a hash, never the token (auth skill).

Description: The user session_version when the session was created.
Why: Rule: a session is valid only while it matches users.session_version.

Description: When the user signed in.
Why: Rule: absolute session lifetime is measured from sign-in.

Description: Last authenticated request, for the idle timeout.
Why: Rule: idle timeout (auth skill).

Description: Absolute end of the session.
Why: Rule: every session ends (auth skill).

Description: Set on sign-out, null while the session is usable.
Why: AC-US-00-011-1: sign-out must end the session on the server.

Description: The caller, so a key is scoped to its user.
Why: Rule: a creating request repeated by a double tap or a network retry makes no second row (api/openapi.yaml Idempotency-Key).

Description: The UUID the client made once per logical operation.
Why: Rule: the same key and body replays the first result for 24 hours (api/openapi.yaml).

Description: Which creating route the key was used on.
Why: Rule: AC-US-00-001-1, AC-US-00-002-1 and AC-US-00-007-1 are the three creating routes, so a key cannot be replayed on another.

Description: SHA-256 of the request body, or of the file bytes for an upload.
Why: Rule: a reused key with a different body is refused with 409, which needs the first body's hash.

Description: Status of the first response, null while it still runs.
Why: Rule: a replay returns the first status, and null tells a concurrent retry the first request is not finished.

Description: Id of the import, document or decision the first request created.
Why: Rule: a replay re-reads the created resource, so no response body and no personal data is stored.

Description: When the first request arrived.
Why: Rule: keys expire after 24 hours, which needs the creation time.

Description: Surrogate key.
Why: AC-US-00-009-1: every export is one row, so the log has a stable id.

Description: The staff member who downloaded the file.
Why: Rule: threat T-23, one request can dump every verified applicant, so who exported is recorded.

Description: Number of Verified applications in the file.
Why: AC-US-00-009-2: an empty export is a header-only file, recorded as zero rows.

Description: When the export ran.
Why: Rule: threat T-23, when an export happened is part of the audit entry.

Description: Surrogate key.
Why: AC-US-00-001-1: an import is one run.

Description: The staff member who ran the import.
Why: Rule: audit who imported; RESTRICT so a user with history cannot be deleted.

Description: File name as uploaded.
Why: AC-US-00-001-2: the user sees which file a reason refers to.

Description: Data rows in the file, header excluded.
Why: AC-US-00-001-3: valid and malformed rows are both reported, so the total is kept.

Description: Rows that became applications.
Why: AC-US-00-001-3: the valid rows are created and counted.

Description: Rows refused, each listed in import_row_errors.
Why: AC-US-00-001-3: the malformed rows are listed with reasons.

Description: When the import ran.
Why: Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Surrogate key.
Why: Rule: bigint identity for a small child table.

Description: The import this error belongs to.
Why: AC-US-00-001-3: errors are shown with their import. CASCADE so they go with it.

Description: Line number in the file, counting the header as line 1.
Why: AC-US-00-001-2: a refused row is shown by its row number.

Description: The column at fault, null when the whole row is.
Why: AC-US-00-001-2: the reason names the column.

Description: Closed set of reasons, including out_of_range and malformed_row for what the database refuses. The offending value is not stored so no personal data enters this table.
Why: AC-US-00-001-2: a reason is shown, and storing a code avoids copying a minor's data.

Description: Surrogate key used in URLs.
Why: AC-US-00-006-2: an application is opened by id.

Description: The import that created this record, null if the import log is purged.
Why: AC-US-00-001-1: records trace to their import. SET NULL so purging the log keeps applicants.

Description: The application id from the CSV, unique.
Why: AC-US-00-001-2: a duplicate application id is refused, and the export is keyed by it (AC-US-00-009-1).

Description: Applicant name as supplied.
Why: AC-US-00-004-1: names are compared with the document.

Description: Father name as supplied.
Why: AC-US-00-004-1: father name is compared on marksheets and transfer certificates.

Description: Date of birth, a minor in most records.
Why: AC-US-00-004-2: dates are compared exactly.

Description: Examination board name.
Why: AC-US-00-001-1: board is one of the eight import columns.

Description: Roll number on the marksheet.
Why: AC-US-00-004-3: roll numbers are compared exactly.

Description: Marks by subject as a JSON object of subject to integer.
Why: AC-US-00-004-4: marks are compared per subject, and the subject set varies by board.

Description: Admission category, a community attribute.
Why: AC-US-00-001-1: category is one of the eight import columns.

Description: verified, needs_review or missing_documents, exactly one at all times.
Why: AC-US-00-005-5: an application is always exactly one of the three. Stored because the dashboard and export read it (AC-US-00-008-1).

Description: Set when a verifier rejects. The application stays needs_review but leaves the queue.
Why: AC-US-00-007-4: a rejected application leaves the flagged queue (Q-006).

Description: Set when the personal columns were replaced by placeholders after an erasure request. The row stays so the decision log keeps its parent.
Why: Rule: erase in place when a table must be kept (privacy-review): decisions reference the application (AC-US-00-007-5).

Description: When the record was imported.
Why: Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Last status or data change, orders the review queue.
Why: AC-US-00-006-1: the queue lists flagged applications in a stable order.

Description: Surrogate key used in URLs.
Why: AC-US-00-006-2: a document is opened by id.

Description: The application this document belongs to. Documents go with their application.
Why: AC-US-00-002-1: a document is stored against an application. CASCADE because documents are the applicant's personal data.

Description: The staff member who uploaded it.
Why: Rule: audit who uploaded; RESTRICT so a user with history cannot be deleted.

Description: image/jpeg, image/png or application/pdf, the only accepted formats.
Why: AC-US-00-002-2: other formats are refused, so the accepted set is closed.

Description: Document type found by the engine, null until processed, unknown if not recognised.
Why: AC-US-00-003-2: a type is stored and an unknown type sends the application to Needs review.

Description: uploaded, processing, read or failed.
Why: AC-US-00-003-1: each document is processed once, so its state is tracked.

Description: A short reason code when processing failed, never document content.
Why: AC-US-02-001-4: a refused or failed call sends the document to Needs review with a reason.

Description: False once a newer document of the same type replaced it. The older one is kept.
Why: AC-US-00-002-4: a re-upload is used for matching and the older one is kept (Q-010).

Description: SHA-256 of the uploaded bytes, hex, to spot a repeated upload.
Why: AC-US-00-002-4: a repeated upload can be recognised without comparing images.

Description: Size of the uploaded file in bytes, at most 8 MiB.
Why: AC-US-00-002-2: files over the limit are refused before they reach the database.

Description: When the file was uploaded.
Why: AC-US-00-002-4: newer means later upload time.

Description: Last status change.
Why: Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: The document these bytes belong to, one-to-one.
Why: AC-US-00-006-2: the review screen shows the document image.

Description: image/png or image/jpeg. A PDF is stored as its first page rasterised to JPEG at no more than 200 dpi so it stays under the size cap. The original PDF is not kept.
Why: AC-US-00-002-3: only the first page of a PDF is rasterised and kept.

Description: The image bytes.
Why: AC-US-00-006-2: the image is shown beside the application values. Kept in Postgres behind a storage interface (ADR-0007).

Description: Surrogate key.
Why: Rule: bigint identity for a small child table.

Description: The document the value was read from.
Why: AC-US-00-003-3: fields are held per document. CASCADE because they are derived from it.

Description: Which field: name, father_name, dob, board, roll_number, marks or document_number.
Why: AC-US-00-004-1 to AC-US-00-004-4: each field type has its own rule.

Description: The subject for a marks row, null for every other field.
Why: AC-US-00-004-4: a mismatch names the subject, so marks are one row per subject.

Description: The current value, after any verifier correction. The value the engine read is kept in the decisions row of the correction.
Why: AC-US-00-003-3: the extracted value is stored as read; AC-US-00-007-2: a correction changes it and logs old and new.

Description: Engine confidence for the lines the value came from, 0 to 1, null when not available.
Why: AC-US-00-003-4: a field below the cutoff goes to Needs review (ADR-0005).

Description: Where the value sits on the page, for the side-by-side view and field crops.
Why: AC-US-00-010-1: a crop of the field is shown beside its value.

Description: match, mismatch or skipped against the application value, null until compared.
Why: AC-US-00-004-5: a field the document type does not carry is skipped, not a mismatch.

Description: True when the field sends the application to Needs review.
Why: AC-US-00-005-2: a mismatch or low-confidence field flags the application.

Description: low_confidence, format_invalid, mismatch or not_extracted, set exactly when needs_review is true.
Why: AC-US-00-006-3: the fields that failed are marked, with the reason (ADR-0005).

Description: When the field was read.
Why: Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Last correction or comparison.
Why: AC-US-00-007-2: a correction re-runs the comparison and updates the row.

Description: Surrogate key.
Why: Rule: bigint identity for an append-only log.

Description: The document read, null if the document was deleted. The call stays counted.
Why: AC-US-02-001-4: the call cap counts every call, so a deleted document must not reduce it.

Description: Engine name, for example rapidocr.
Why: AC-US-02-001-3: each call logs its engine.

Description: Engine and model version, so a result can be traced to what produced it.
Why: AC-US-02-001-3: the log is how an engine swap is audited.

Description: Whether the OpenCV preprocessing ran first.
Why: ADR-0001: preprocessing is part of the chosen engine, so the log records it.

Description: Longest image side in pixels after the cap, null if none.
Why: ADR-0001: the 640 px cap changes memory, so it is logged.

Description: Wall time of the call in milliseconds.
Why: AC-US-02-001-3: latency is logged per call.

Description: pending while the engine runs, then ok or error, or refused when the call cap was reached. The pending row is committed before the call so the call is logged even if the process dies.
Why: AC-US-02-001-3 and AC-US-02-001-4: every call is logged, including one that never returned, and a refused call is recorded.

Description: Text lines returned, the unit count the gateway logs.
Why: AC-US-02-001-3: unit counts are logged.

Description: Always zero: no paid engine is allowed.
Why: AC-US-02-001-3: cost is logged as 0 (CONSTRAINTS.md section 1).

Description: Exception class name on failure, never a message that could hold document text.
Why: AC-US-02-001-3: the outcome is logged without personal data (AC-US-00-004 privacy case TC-0023).

Description: When the call was made.
Why: AC-US-02-001-4: the cap window and the log are ordered by time.

Description: Surrogate key.
Why: AC-US-00-007-5: each decision is one log entry.

Description: The application decided. RESTRICT so the record cannot disappear with it.
Why: AC-US-00-007-5: the log must outlive routine changes to the application.

Description: The verifier who decided.
Why: AC-US-00-007-5: the entry holds who decided.

Description: For a correction, the exact field of the exact document that was changed. Null for approve and reject, and null after the document is erased.
Why: AC-US-00-007-2: an application can have a name on several documents, so a correction must say which one it changed.

Description: approve, correct or reject.
Why: AC-US-00-007-1 to AC-US-00-007-4: three actions.

Description: Required for a reject, free text a verifier typed.
Why: AC-US-00-007-3: a rejection without a reason is refused.

Description: For a correction, the field changed.
Why: AC-US-00-007-2: a correction logs which value changed.

Description: For a marks correction, the subject.
Why: AC-US-00-007-2: a marks correction names the subject.

Description: For a correction, the value before.
Why: AC-US-00-007-2: the old value is logged.

Description: For a correction, the value after.
Why: AC-US-00-007-2: the new value is logged.

Description: When the decision was made.
Why: AC-US-00-007-5: the entry holds when.
